15		"golang.org/x/mod/semver"
16	)

18	// Host-agnostic remote inspection over the git protocol. Version listing
19	// uses `git ls-remote --tags`, which behaves identically on GitHub, GitLab,
20	// Gitea/Forgejo, and any self-hosted server, inherits the user's existing
21	// git auth (SSH agent, credential helpers), and needs no forge REST client.
22	// The shell-out (vs go-git) is deliberate: this path needs the user's
23	// credential helpers and proxy config, the same reason hooks.go shells out
24	// for network-touching operations.
25	
26	// pluginGitTimeout bounds any single git subprocess this package spawns.
27	// Without it these calls are unbounded: the root context is WithCancel, not
28	// WithTimeout, so a black-holed host hangs the command with no output. That
29	// matters most during dependency planning, which issues one ls-remote plus up
30	// to two shallow clones per dependency against author-controlled URLs, before
31	// the user has confirmed anything. The asset download already caps at 5
32	// minutes; this is the git half of the same bound.
33	const pluginGitTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
34	
35	// runGitQuiet runs git and returns stdout, with a bounded deadline and an
36	// environment that cannot block on a prompt.
37	//
38	// Output() (not Run()) so stderr lands in the ExitError for error messages.
39	// LC_ALL=C/LANG=C keep git's messages in English: fetchPluginMetadataAtTag decides
40	// the benign "no metadata file" case by substring-matching git's stderr, and
41	// git builds with NLS translate those strings — on a localized host every
42	// plugin repo without an entire-plugin.yml (the documented default) would
43	// otherwise fail to install. BatchMode stops ssh prompting for a key
44	// passphrase on /dev/tty, which GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT does not cover — but only
45	// when the user has not set GIT_SSH_COMMAND themselves.
46	func runGitQuiet(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
47		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, pluginGitTimeout)
48		defer cancel()
49		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
50		env := append(os.Environ(), "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0", "LC_ALL=C", "LANG=C")
51		// Only supply a batch-mode ssh when the user has not configured one. A
52		// blanket GIT_SSH_COMMAND would override both the env var and
53		// core.sshCommand, discarding a custom ssh invocation (jump hosts, an
54		// explicit identity) and breaking clones that only work through it.
55		// Respecting an existing setting costs the passphrase-prompt guard in that
56		// one case, which is the right trade — the user chose that command.
57		if _, set := os.LookupEnv("GIT_SSH_COMMAND"); !set {
58			env = append(env, "GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -oBatchMode=yes")
59		}
60		cmd.Env = env
61		out, err := cmd.Output()
62		if err != nil {
63			// Wrapped by callers with the operation and (redacted) URL; the bare
64			// verb here keeps the deadline case legible.
65			return out, fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w", args[0], err)
66		}
67		return out, nil
68	}

95	// transport chooses the binary. That is strictly worse than the plaintext-asset
96	// case the download path already refuses.
97	var gitURLSchemes = []string{"https://", "ssh://", "file://"}

99	// scpLikeGitURL matches git's scp-like syntax (user@host:path) — the form
100	// `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` uses. Requires a user@, a host without a
101	// slash, and a colon before the path, so it cannot match a bare option or a
102	// local path.
103	var scpLikeGitURL = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:[^\s]`)
104	
105	// validatePluginRepoURL rejects anything that is not recognizably a git
106	// repository URL before it reaches the git CLI as a positional argument.
107	//
108	// This is a security boundary, not a nicety. These URLs arrive from
109	// attacker-influenced places — index.json entries, another plugin's
110	// entire-plugin.yml requires[], a stored manifest, --index — and git parses an
111	// option-shaped positional as an option. `--upload-pack=<cmd>` is
112	// shell-interpreted and runs against the *ambient* repo when no positional
113	// remains, so an entry like "--upload-pack=curl … | sh; git-upload-pack" would
114	// execute arbitrary commands during an index-resolved install, which never
115	// prompts. validatePluginName already refuses a leading '-' on names for the
116	// same reason.
117	//
118	// Bare absolute paths are rejected: file:// expresses the same thing
119	// unambiguously, and narrowing a security boundary beats the convenience.
120	// Callers additionally pass "--" before positionals, so an option-shaped value
121	// would be refused by git even if it got this far.
122	func validatePluginRepoURL(rawURL string) error {
123		u := strings.TrimSpace(rawURL)
124		if u == "" {
125			return errors.New("repository URL is empty")
126		}
127		if strings.HasPrefix(u, "-") {
128			return fmt.Errorf("repository URL %q must not start with '-'", redactURL(rawURL))
129		}
130		for _, scheme := range gitURLSchemes {
131			if strings.HasPrefix(u, scheme) && len(u) > len(scheme) {
132				return nil
133			}
134		}
135		if scpLikeGitURL.MatchString(u) {
136			return nil
137		}
138		return fmt.Errorf("repository URL %q must use one of %s or git's user@host:path form",

140	}

142	// listRemoteSemverTags returns the repo's semver tags ("v"-prefixed or
143	// bare), sorted descending by semantic version. Non-semver tags are
144	// ignored.
145	func listRemoteSemverTags(ctx context.Context, repoURL string) ([]string, error) {
146		if err := validatePluginRepoURL(repoURL); err != nil {
147			return nil, err
148		}
149		// --refs suppresses peeled ^{} entries for annotated tags. "--" keeps an
150		// option-shaped URL from being parsed as a git option.
151		out, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, "ls-remote", "--tags", "--refs", "--", repoURL)
152		if err != nil {
153			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list tags of %s: %w%s", redactURL(repoURL), err, stderrSuffix(err))
154		}
155		var tags []string
156		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
157			fields := strings.Fields(line)
158			if len(fields) != 2 {
159				continue
160			}
161			tag := strings.TrimPrefix(fields[1], "refs/tags/")
162			canon := canonicalSemver(tag)
163			if !semver.IsValid(canon) {
164				continue
165			}
166			// Prereleases are excluded: semver ranks v2.0.0-rc1 above stable
167			// v1.9.0, so an author pushing a release candidate would migrate every
168			// user onto it on the next `plugin upgrade --all`. --pin installs an
169			// exact tag and bypasses this listing, which is the opt-in.
170			if semver.Prerelease(canon) != "" {
171				continue
172			}
173			tags = append(tags, tag)
174		}
175		// Stable, so tags that compare equal (v1.0.0 vs 1.0.0, or +build metadata,
176		// which semver ignores) resolve in a deterministic order.
177		sort.SliceStable(tags, func(i, j int) bool {
178			return semver.Compare(canonicalSemver(tags[i]), canonicalSemver(tags[j])) > 0
179		})
180		return tags, nil
181	}
182	
183	// canonicalSemver maps a tag to the "v"-prefixed form x/mod/semver expects.
184	func canonicalSemver(tag string) string {
185		if strings.HasPrefix(tag, "v") {
186			return tag
187		}
188		return "v" + tag
189	}
190	
191	// stderrSuffix extracts captured stderr from an exec.ExitError for error
192	// messages; git's stderr is where the actionable detail lives. Only
193	// populated when the command was started via Output().
194	func stderrSuffix(err error) string {
195		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
196		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && len(exitErr.Stderr) > 0 {
197			return ": " + redactCredentials(strings.TrimSpace(string(exitErr.Stderr)))
198		}
199		return ""
200	}
201	
202	// fetchPluginMetadataAtTag reads entire-plugin.yml at the given tag without
203	// a user-visible clone: a blobless shallow clone into a discarded temp dir,
204	// falling back to a plain shallow clone for servers that don't allow
205	// partial-clone filters (uploadpack.allowFilter defaults to off outside the
206	// big forges). Returns (nil, nil) when the repo has no metadata file —
207	// metadata is optional by design.
208	func fetchPluginMetadataAtTag(ctx context.Context, repoURL, tag string) (*PluginMetadata, error) {
209		if err := validatePluginRepoURL(repoURL); err != nil {
210			return nil, err
211		}
212		tmp, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "entire-plugin-meta-")
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create temp dir: %w", err)
215		}
216		defer os.RemoveAll(tmp)
217	
218		cloneArgs := func(filter bool) []string {
219			args := []string{"clone", "--depth", "1", "--no-checkout", "--branch", tag, "--quiet"}
220			if filter {
221				args = append(args, "--filter=blob:none")
222			}
223			// "--" so an option-shaped URL can't be parsed as a git option.
224			return append(args, "--", repoURL, tmp)
225		}
226		// Output() (not Run()) so stderr is captured into the ExitError for
227		// error messages; clone --quiet writes nothing to stdout.
228		if _, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, cloneArgs(true)...); err != nil {
229			// Retry without the filter; the clone dir may be half-created.
230			if rmErr := os.RemoveAll(tmp); rmErr != nil {
231				return nil, fmt.Errorf("clean temp clone dir: %w", rmErr)
232			}
233			if _, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, cloneArgs(false)...); err != nil {
234				return nil, fmt.Errorf("clone %s at %s: %w%s", redactURL(repoURL), tag, err, stderrSuffix(err))
235			}
236		}
237		// `git show <rev>:<path>` peels annotated tags and, in a blobless
238		// clone, lazily fetches just this one blob from the promisor remote.
239		out, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, "-C", tmp, "show", tag+":"+pluginMetadataFileName)
240		if err != nil {
241			// Missing file and missing tag both surface as exit 128; only the
242			// missing-file case is benign. Disambiguate via stderr.
243			if strings.Contains(stderrSuffix(err), "does not exist") ||
244				strings.Contains(stderrSuffix(err), "exists on disk, but not in") {
245				return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // metadata is optional
246			}
247			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s at %s: %w%s", pluginMetadataFileName, tag, err, stderrSuffix(err))
248		}
249		return ParsePluginMetadata(out)
250	}
251	
252	// pluginNameFromRepoURL derives the bare plugin name from a repository URL
253	// basename: .../entire-run(.git) → "run". Used when entire-plugin.yml is
254	// absent or doesn't declare a name.
255	func pluginNameFromRepoURL(repoURL string) (string, error) {
256		trimmed := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(repoURL, "/"), ".git")
257		base := trimmed
258		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(trimmed, "/:"); i >= 0 {
259			base = trimmed[i+1:]
260		}
261		if !strings.HasPrefix(base, pluginBinaryPrefix) {
262			return "", fmt.Errorf("repository basename %q does not start with %q; declare a name in %s", base, pluginBinaryPrefix, pluginMetadataFileName)
263		}
264		name := strings.TrimPrefix(base, pluginBinaryPrefix)
265		if err := validatePluginName(name); err != nil {
266			return "", err
267		}
268		return name, nil
269	}

21	// Plugin discovery rides on a git-synced index, krew-style: the index is
22	// itself a git repository containing index.json, shallow-cloned into the
23	// user cache and re-pulled on a TTL. No hosted service, no forge REST API —
24	// any git server can host an index. An organization points the CLI at an
25	// internal catalog with ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL or --index; see
26	// resolvePluginIndexURL for why a committed settings file cannot.
27	const (
28		// defaultPluginIndexURL is the built-in curated index.
29		defaultPluginIndexURL = "https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index"
30		// pluginIndexEnvVar overrides the index URL (forwarded to plugin
31		// children automatically via the ENTIRE_ allowlist prefix).
32		pluginIndexEnvVar = "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL"
33		// pluginIndexFileName is the catalog file at the index repo root.
34		pluginIndexFileName = "index.json"
35		// pluginIndexSchemaVersion is the index schema this CLI reads. Advisory:
36		// a higher declared version logs a warning and is still read (see
37		// loadPluginIndexFromDir).
38		pluginIndexSchemaVersion = 1
39		// pluginIndexSyncMarker records the last successful sync time as the
40		// marker file's mtime. Untracked, so fetch/reset never touches it.
41		pluginIndexSyncMarker = ".entire-last-sync"

43		// rather than configurable: `plugin index update` already forces a refresh
44		// and stale-on-offline already covers a failed one, so a knob here tuned a
45		// problem solved twice over while costing a settings load per sync.

49	// PluginIndex is the parsed catalog. Decoding is deliberately lenient
50	// (unknown fields ignored) so an index that grows new fields doesn't break
51	// older CLI versions fleet-wide.
52	type PluginIndex struct {
53		// Version is the declared schema version. Advisory only — see
54		// loadPluginIndexFromDir for why it isn't enforced.
55		Version int                `json:"version"`
56		Plugins []PluginIndexEntry `json:"plugins"`
57	}
58	
59	// PluginIndexEntry describes one plugin in the catalog.
60	type PluginIndexEntry struct {
61		Name        string `json:"name"`
62		RepoURL     string `json:"repo_url"`
63		Description string `json:"description,omitempty"`
64		Official    bool   `json:"official,omitempty"`
65		// Platforms lists supported GOOS values when the plugin doesn't ship
66		// the full matrix; empty means all.

70	// Find returns the entry with the given bare name, or nil.
71	func (idx *PluginIndex) Find(name string) *PluginIndexEntry {
72		if idx == nil {
73			return nil
74		}
75		for i := range idx.Plugins {
76			if idx.Plugins[i].Name == name {
77				return &idx.Plugins[i]

83	// Search returns entries whose name or description contains term
84	// (case-insensitive). An empty term returns everything.
85	func (idx *PluginIndex) Search(term string) []PluginIndexEntry {
86		if idx == nil {
87			return nil
88		}
89		if term == "" {
90			return idx.Plugins
91		}
92		t := strings.ToLower(term)
93		var out []PluginIndexEntry
94		for _, e := range idx.Plugins {
95			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name), t) || strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Description), t) {
96				out = append(out, e)
97			}
98		}
99		return out

102	// HasRepoURL reports whether a repo URL is listed in the index — the trust
103	// check for install confirmations. Compared with the .git suffix and
104	// trailing slashes normalized.
105	func (idx *PluginIndex) HasRepoURL(repoURL string) bool {
106		if idx == nil {
107			return false
108		}
109		want := normalizeRepoURL(repoURL)
110		for _, e := range idx.Plugins {
111			if normalizeRepoURL(e.RepoURL) == want {
112				return true
113			}
114		}
115		return false

118	func normalizeRepoURL(u string) string {
119		return strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(u), "/"), ".git")
120	}

122	// resolvePluginIndexURL applies the documented precedence: --index flag >
123	// ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL > built-in default.
124	//
125	// Repo-level settings are deliberately NOT a source. .entire/settings.json is a
126	// committed file resolved from the working directory, and an index-listed repo
127	// installs with no confirmation prompt — so honoring it there meant a cloned
128	// repository could redirect the catalog and get an attacker-chosen binary
129	// downloaded, chmod 0755, and linked onto the user's PATH without a prompt.
130	// The value of that setting was precisely that contributors got a different
131	// catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature; it
132	// cannot be kept and made safe, only removed or made visible.
133	//
134	// Organizations wanting an internal catalog set ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL, which
135	// applies across repos rather than per-repo, and cannot be chosen by content
136	// the user merely checked out. This matches Go, where no repo-committed file
137	// can redirect GOPROXY; npm's per-project registry override is the
138	// cautionary counter-example.
139	func resolvePluginIndexURL(flagValue string) string {
140		if flagValue != "" {
141			return flagValue
142		}
143		if v := os.Getenv(pluginIndexEnvVar); v != "" {
144			return v
145		}
146		return defaultPluginIndexURL
147	}

149	// pluginIndexCacheDir is the per-URL local copy. Keyed by a hash of the
150	// URL so switching indexes (or per-repo overrides) never serves one
151	// catalog's cache for another.
152	func pluginIndexCacheDir(indexURL string) (string, error) {
153		cache := userdirs.Cache()
154		if cache == "" {
155			return "", errors.New("cannot resolve user cache directory")
156		}
157		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(normalizeRepoURL(indexURL)))
158		return filepath.Join(cache, "plugin-index", hex.EncodeToString(sum[:6])), nil
159	}

161	// SyncPluginIndex returns the catalog for indexURL, cloning or refreshing
162	// the local copy as needed. force bypasses the TTL. When a refresh fails
163	// but a previous copy exists, the stale copy is used with a warning logged
164	// — discovery shouldn't hard-fail because a laptop is offline.
165	func SyncPluginIndex(ctx context.Context, indexURL string, force bool) (*PluginIndex, error) {
166		// The index URL reaches `git clone` as a positional; it can come from
167		// --index or ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL, neither of which the settings
168		// validator sees. Reject non-URLs before git can read one as an option.
169		if err := validatePluginRepoURL(indexURL); err != nil {
170			return nil, fmt.Errorf("plugin index URL: %w", err)
171		}
172		dir, err := pluginIndexCacheDir(indexURL)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, err
175		}
176	
177		// The cache dir is shared by every concurrent `entire plugin` invocation
178		// and syncing it is destructive: RemoveAll + clone on the cold path,
179		// fetch + `reset --hard FETCH_HEAD` on the warm one. Serialize the whole
180		// sync-and-read under an advisory lock, the same way discovery/cache.go
181		// guards its shared cache files. Without it, one process cloning while
182		// another reads index.json surfaces a spurious "no readable index.json",
183		// and two cold syncs racing can leave exactly the half-created directory
184		// the sweep below exists to recover from.
185		//
186		// The lock file is a *sibling* of the cache dir, not inside it: RemoveAll
187		// on the dir would otherwise delete the lock file while we hold it.
188		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dir), 0o750); err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create index cache dir: %w", err)
190		}
191		release, err := flock.AcquireContext(ctx, dir+".lock")
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, fmt.Errorf("lock plugin index cache: %w", err)
194		}
195		defer release()

197		marker := filepath.Join(dir, pluginIndexSyncMarker)
198		_, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"))
199		cloned := statErr == nil
200	
201		fresh := false
202		if cloned && !force {
203			if info, err := os.Stat(marker); err == nil {
204				// A negative age means the marker is dated in the future (clock
205				// rollback, restored backup, bad container clock). Treating that as
206				// fresh would freeze the catalog until someone ran `index update`
207				// by hand, so only a non-negative age inside the window counts.
208				if age := time.Since(info.ModTime()); age >= 0 && age < pluginIndexTTL {
209					fresh = true
210				}
211			}
212		}
213	
214		switch {
215		case !cloned:
216			// A previously interrupted clone can leave a partial directory
217			// without .git. git refuses to clone into a non-empty target, so
218			// without this sweep, discovery would stay wedged until the user
219			// cleared the cache by hand.
220			if err := os.RemoveAll(dir); err != nil {
221				return nil, fmt.Errorf("clear stale index cache: %w", err)

231			} else {
232				touchFile(marker)
233			}
234		}
235	
236		return loadPluginIndexFromDir(ctx, dir, indexURL)
237	}

239	// refreshPluginIndexClone updates an existing shallow clone to the remote
240	// tip regardless of the remote's default branch name.
241	func refreshPluginIndexClone(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
242		if _, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, "-C", dir, "fetch", "--depth", "1", "--quiet", "origin", "HEAD"); err != nil {
243			return fmt.Errorf("fetch: %w%s", err, stderrSuffix(err))
244		}
245		if _, err := runGitQuiet(ctx, "-C", dir, "reset", "--hard", "--quiet", "FETCH_HEAD"); err != nil {
246			return fmt.Errorf("reset: %w%s", err, stderrSuffix(err))
247		}
248		return nil
249	}

251	func touchFile(path string) {
252		now := time.Now()
253		if err := os.Chtimes(path, now, now); err == nil {
254			return
255		}
256		if f, err := os.Create(path); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // marker file inside our cache dir
257			_ = f.Close()
258		}
259	}

261	func loadPluginIndexFromDir(ctx context.Context, dir, indexURL string) (*PluginIndex, error) {
262		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, pluginIndexFileName)) //nolint:gosec // file inside our cache dir
263		if err != nil {
264			return nil, fmt.Errorf("plugin index %s has no readable %s: %w", redactURL(indexURL), pluginIndexFileName, err)
265		}
266		var idx PluginIndex
267		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &idx); err != nil {
268			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse %s from %s: %w", pluginIndexFileName, redactURL(indexURL), err)
269		}
270		// version is recorded, not enforced. Refusing an unrecognized value would
271		// protect against a migration that can never happen: the index is one
272		// shared resource read by every CLI version ever shipped, so bumping it
273		// would break discovery fleet-wide with no gradual rollout and no undo for
274		// installed binaries. An incompatible schema therefore ships at a new path
275		// (index-v2.json, another branch, another repo), which needs no gate here.
276		// Enforcing it only ever fired by accident — most painfully on an index
277		// that simply omits the field (version 0), which told the author to
278		// upgrade the CLI when the fix was in their own file. Hand-written
279		// internal catalogs are a first-class case (ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL).
280		//
281		// Additive changes, the ones that actually happen, are already absorbed:
282		// decoding ignores unknown fields and unreadable entries are dropped
283		// below. Degrading per entry beats refusing the catalog.
284		if idx.Version > pluginIndexSchemaVersion {
285			logging.Warn(ctx, "plugin index declares a newer schema version; reading what this CLI understands",
286				slog.String("index", redactURL(indexURL)),
287				slog.Int("declared_version", idx.Version),
288				slog.Int("understood_version", pluginIndexSchemaVersion))
289		}
290		var valid []PluginIndexEntry
291		for _, e := range idx.Plugins {
292			// repo_url is validated here, not just at the git boundary: an
293			// index-resolved install is treated as trusted and never prompts, so
294			// a hostile catalog entry must not reach the git CLI at all.
295			if validatePluginName(e.Name) != nil || validatePluginRepoURL(e.RepoURL) != nil {
296				continue // tolerate bad entries rather than failing the catalog
297			}
298			valid = append(valid, e)
299		}
300		idx.Plugins = valid
301		return &idx, nil
302	}

128	// ParsePluginMetadata decodes entire-plugin.yml content.
129	//

131	// index.json. Both are artifacts read by every CLI version ever shipped, and
132	// refusing one an older binary doesn't fully understand breaks it permanently
133	// for everyone on that version — the plugin author cannot fix it for them.
134	// entire-plugin.yml has no version field to gate on either, so the first author
135	// to adopt any future field (min_cli_version, bin_name, …) would break installs

139	// did. The trade is asymmetric: a misspelled key costs the author one confused

141	// unfixable and fleet-wide. Author-side validation belongs in a lint command,
142	// not in the hot path every user's install runs through.
143	func ParsePluginMetadata(data []byte) (*PluginMetadata, error) {

148			// documented as optional and a *missing* one is fine, so a committed
149			// placeholder must not be fatal at every tag. An explicit "---" already
150			// behaved this way; align the empty cases with it.

163				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s declares invalid requirement: %w", pluginMetadataFileName, err)
164			}
165			// A malformed min_version silently removes the floor rather than
166			// failing: x/mod/semver ranks an invalid string below every valid one,
167			// so semver.Compare(installedTag, garbage) >= 0 is always true and
168			// dependencySatisfied reports any version as acceptable. "vtypo",
169			// "latest" and ">=1.0" all behave that way.
170			//

172			// tension with it. Unknown *keys* stay lenient because they are a newer
173			// CLI's fields and refusing them breaks older binaries permanently. A
174			// malformed *value of a known field* is an author error that no CLI
175			// version will ever accept — which is why req.Name is already validated
176			// right here.
177			if req.MinVersion != "" && !semver.IsValid(canonicalSemver(req.MinVersion)) {
178				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s requirement %q declares invalid min_version %q: want a semver tag such as v0.2.0 (a minimum only — ranges are not supported)",

180			}

234		// token in a remote URL has no business on disk. Upgrades re-resolve the
235		// remote through git's credential helpers, which is where auth belongs.

247		// after the binary it describes was swapped in.

257	// skipped — a half-removed plugin shouldn't break listing.

283	}

+The two digests are not redundant. `sha256` covers the downloaded asset, which is usually an archive and is discarded with the staging directory — provenance only, nothing left to compare against. `binary_sha256` covers the executable under `pkg/<name>/`, which is what `entire plugin doctor` re-hashes to detect a binary swapped out after install.
+
+Installing from a URL not listed in the index prints the source and asks for confirmation (`--yes` to skip; required in non-interactive runs). Index-listed repos install without prompting — with one exception: `entire plugin browse` confirms its selection. The picker shows only a name and description, and an index-resolved install would otherwise proceed unprompted, so highlighting a row and pressing Enter would download a binary and link it onto `PATH` in a single keystroke. The confirmation names the repository the binary comes from.
+
+#### Repository URLs are a security boundary
+
+Every repo URL is validated by `validatePluginRepoURL` before it reaches the git CLI, and every git invocation passes `--` before its positionals. Both layers exist because repo URLs are attacker-influenced: they arrive from `index.json` entries and from `--index`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`.
+
+git parses an option-shaped positional as an option, and `--upload-pack=<cmd>` is shell-interpreted — with no positional repository left, it runs against the *ambient* repo's `origin`. So a catalog entry like `--upload-pack=curl … | sh; git-upload-pack` would execute arbitrary commands during an index-resolved install, which by design never prompts. Dependency planning is the tightest path: it contacts a dependency's repository — now always an index-listed one — *before* the install confirmation.
+
+Accepted forms are `https://`, `ssh://`, `file://`, and git's `user@host:path` scp-like syntax. Anything else — a leading `-`, a bare name, a relative or bare absolute path, git's command-executing `ext::` transport — is rejected.
+
+`http://` and `git://` are deliberately absent. Both are unauthenticated and unencrypted, and the catalog fetched over them decides which repositories install *without a confirmation prompt*, so an attacker who can rewrite the transport chooses the binary — strictly worse than the plaintext-asset case below. Bare absolute paths are rejected because `file://` expresses the same thing unambiguously; narrowing a security boundary beats the convenience.
+
+The rule has exactly one definition, `validatePluginRepoURL`, applied to plugin repositories and to the index URL alike. Two validators previously disagreed about `http://`, `git://`, and absolute paths, so `--index /srv/idx` was accepted while the equivalent settings value was a hard load failure; the settings key is gone (see below) and one definition remains. Invalid index entries are dropped like invalid names, so one bad row cannot take out the catalog.
+
+This mirrors `validatePluginName`, which refuses a leading `-` on names for the same reason. Regression coverage asserts the payload never executes, not merely that the call errors.
+
+#### `entire-plugin.yml` decodes leniently
+
+Unknown keys are ignored, the same choice made for `index.json` and for the same reason: both are artifacts read by every CLI version ever shipped, and refusing one an older binary doesn't fully understand breaks it permanently for everyone on that version, with no way for the plugin author to fix it for them. `entire-plugin.yml` has no `version` field to gate on either, so the first author to adopt any future field would break installs on every older CLI.
+
+This gives up catching author typos, which strict decoding did. The trade is asymmetric: a misspelled key costs the author one confused test run against their own plugin; a forward-compatibility break is unfixable and fleet-wide. Author-side validation belongs in a lint command, not in the path every user's install runs through.
+
+An empty or comment-only file is also accepted — the file is documented as optional, and a committed placeholder should not be fatal at every tag.
+
+#### The installed name must match what was requested
+
+The installed plugin name comes from the *remote* — `entire-plugin.yml`'s `name:`, else the repository basename. Whenever the caller has already committed to a name, that name is passed down as a required argument to `InstallPluginFromRepo` and a mismatch is fatal. It is an argument rather than an options field deliberately: a field can be silently omitted, and omitting it reopens the hole, whereas passing `""` is a visible choice at the call site. Three paths set it: an index-resolved install (the catalog entry the user typed), a dependency install (the requirement being satisfied), and an upgrade (the plugin being upgraded). A bare `install <url>` sets nothing, because there the repository legitimately names itself.
+
+Unchecked, the remote chose the name unilaterally and three things broke: an index entry named `safe` could install `entire-hijack` with no prompt (index installs never prompt); `--force` escalated across plugins, because the already-installed check tested the remote-declared name, so reinstalling A let A's repo declare `name: B` and replace an unrelated installed B; and a dependency installed under another name never satisfied its requirement, so `doctor` reported it missing forever and every future parent install re-attempted it.
+
+It fails rather than warns: every caller that sets an expectation has already made a trust decision about *that* name, and silently honoring a different one voids it. A genuine rename is a catalog entry or a requirement to fix.
+
+#### Credentials never reach logs, output, or disk
+
+A remote may embed credentials (`REDACTED`). Every path that prints, logs, or persists a repository, index, or **asset download** URL strips the userinfo first, and git's captured stderr is scrubbed for the same pattern.
+
+The download path needs saying explicitly: `releaseAssetBaseURL` derives the asset URL from the repo URL, and `url.String()` re-serializes embedded userinfo, so a private-forge remote produces a credentialed download URL. The request keeps it — that is how it authenticates — but every message goes through `redactURL`, because a download failure is an ordinary event (network hiccup, 5xx, checksum mismatch) and `main.go` prints command errors straight to stderr. This matters more than usual here: `.entire/logs/` lives inside the user's working tree and is collected wholesale by `entire doctor bundle`, and `manifest.yml` is written mode 0644. Upgrades re-resolve auth through git's credential helpers, which is where it belongs.
+
+#### Downloads must be authenticated, over a transport that can't be rewritten
+
+Two requirements apply to every asset fetch, both enforced at the HTTP boundary so the author-declared `download_url` escape hatch is covered as well as the derived forge URLs:
+
+**HTTPS.** Plaintext HTTP is refused for anything off-machine. This isn't stylistic: the asset and the `checksums.txt` that authenticates it come from the same origin, so an attacker who can rewrite one can rewrite both and checksum verification proves nothing. Loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`) is exempt so `httptest` fixtures and local forge experiments keep working — traffic that never leaves the machine has no network attacker to defend against.
+
+The check runs on **every redirect hop**, via the client's `CheckRedirect`, not just the initial URL. Go's default policy follows up to ten redirects and will happily cross from `https` to `http`, so validating only the entry point left the rule bypassable by any release host with an open redirect — the asset *and* its `checksums.txt` could both arrive in plaintext, which is precisely the outcome the rule exists to prevent.
+
+**A checksum manifest.** A release that publishes an asset but no `checksums.txt` covering the platform is refused by default; installing means making those bytes executable, so it takes an explicit `--allow-unverified`. Two shapes are unverifiable and hit the same gate: a release with no manifest at all, and a `download_url` with no `{asset}` placeholder (every candidate name expands to one fixed URL, so no manifest can be located — add `{asset}` to fix it properly).
+
+The candidate probe still runs when verification is required, because it separates two failures that need different handling: *no release published for this tag yet* (`errAssetNotFound` — worth walking down to the next-highest tag) from *release exists but publishes no checksums* (`errUnverifiedAsset` — an older tag wouldn't be any more trustworthy, so the walk stops). Conflating them would report a missing release for a plugin that simply doesn't ship checksums.
+
+An install that used the opt-in is recorded as `unverified: true` in the manifest, reported by `entire plugin doctor` until the author publishes checksums, and inherited by `plugin upgrade` — so a knowingly-unverified plugin doesn't start failing on upgrade, and a verified one can't silently become unverified.
+
+### Plugin index (discovery)
+
+Discovery rides on a git-synced index, krew-style: the index is itself a git repository containing `index.json`, shallow-cloned into the user cache (keyed by a hash of the URL) and refreshed on a TTL. `entire plugin search [term]`, `info <name>`, and `browse` read it; `entire plugin index update` forces a refresh. When a refresh fails but a cached copy exists, the stale copy is used — discovery doesn't hard-fail offline.
+
+The effective index URL resolves as: `--index` flag > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` > the built-in default (`https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index`). Freshness is a fixed 24 hours.
+
+**Repo-level settings are deliberately not a source, and there is no TTL knob.** Both were removed rather than hardened:
+
+`plugins.index_url` was read from `.entire/settings.json` — a committed file resolved from the working directory — while an index-listed repository installs with *no confirmation prompt*. Composed, that meant a cloned repository could redirect the catalog and have an attacker-chosen binary downloaded, `chmod 0755`, and linked onto the user's `PATH` without a prompt. The value of the setting was precisely that contributors got a different catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature: it cannot be kept and made safe, only removed or made visible. Removing it also makes the failure mode safe — a missing override now falls back to the curated default rather than to someone else's catalog.
+
+An organization wanting an internal catalog sets `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`, which applies across repositories rather than per-repository and cannot be chosen by content the user merely checked out. Go takes the same position — no repo-committed file can redirect `GOPROXY` — while npm's per-project `registry` override is the cautionary counter-example.
+
+`plugins.index_ttl_hours` went with it: `entire plugin index update` already forces a refresh and stale-on-offline already covers a failed one, so the knob tuned a problem solved twice while costing a settings load per sync. Between them, the whole `PluginSettings` struct, its validator, its merge path, and its tests are gone — the plugin layer now reads no settings at all.
+
+`index.json` schema (version 1): `{"version": 1, "plugins": [{"name", "repo_url", "description", "official", "platforms"}]}`. Entries with invalid names (e.g. the reserved `agent-` prefix) or unusable repo URLs are filtered on load, not fatal.
+
+`version` is **recorded, not enforced**: an index declaring a newer version (or omitting the field) still loads, logging a warning. Gating on it would guard a migration that can never happen — the index is one shared resource read by every CLI version ever shipped, so bumping it would break discovery fleet-wide with no gradual rollout and no undo for installed binaries. An incompatible schema therefore ships at a new path (`index-v2.json`, another branch, another repo). Meanwhile the changes that do happen are already absorbed: decoding ignores unknown fields, so new fields are free, and unreadable entries are dropped individually. Degrading per entry beats refusing the catalog — a company's hand-written internal index that forgets `"version"` should not be told to upgrade the CLI.
+
+### Dependencies
+
+A plugin declares dependencies in `entire-plugin.yml`:
+
+```yaml
+name: brain
+requires:
+  - name: graph          # resolved by name through the plugin index
+    min_version: v0.2.0  # minimum only; no ranges, and validated at parse
+```
+
+`min_version` is checked for well-formedness when the metadata is parsed. A malformed value would otherwise *remove* the floor rather than fail: `x/mod/semver` ranks an invalid string below every valid one, so the comparison in `dependencySatisfied` reports any installed version as acceptable — `vtypo`, `latest` and `>=1.0` all behave that way. Rejecting a malformed value of a known field is consistent with the lenient decoding above, which is about unknown *keys*: those are a newer CLI's fields and refusing them breaks older binaries permanently, whereas a bad version string is an author error no CLI version will ever accept.
+
+**A requirement carries no URL.** A missing dependency resolves by name through the index and nowhere else, so the URL a dependency install fetches from always comes from the curated catalog rather than from the requiring plugin's author. With an author-supplied `repo_url`, installing one plugin meant fetching and executing a binary from a URL its author chose — and planning contacted that URL *before* the confirmation prompt.
+
+The capability is not gone, the authority moved: a user can still install an out-of-catalog dependency by URL themselves, with the usual untrusted-source prompt, after which the requirement is satisfied and planning schedules nothing. Consent belongs to the user, not the plugin author.
+
+The consequence is a publishing order — a dependency must be indexed before a dependent can ship — which is the same constraint krew, Homebrew and apt impose. A `repo_url` left over from the old schema is ignored rather than honored, since `entire-plugin.yml` decodes leniently, so previously-published files keep parsing and simply lose the URL.
+
+Resolution is **install-time only** — dispatch stays zero-cost. The outcome is verified, not just the attempt: an install that lands below the requirement's `min_version` fails with both versions named, because the install takes the newest published tag and that tag may still be too old. Reporting success there would defeat the guarantee the plan was built on. After installing the main plugin, missing dependencies are resolved transitively (metadata-only, nothing downloaded during planning; a per-name record of the strictest `min_version` seen, plus a depth bound, make metadata cycles an error rather than a hang), listed apt-style, and installed after one confirmation (`--yes` skips, `--no-deps` opts out). A declined plan is a warning, not a failure. Dependencies already satisfied from raw `$PATH` or a local-dev install count as satisfied, with a warning when `min_version` can't be verified.
